companies.name: Nudge
companies.funding_note: $100M Series A led by Thrive Capital and Greenoaks. DATE CONFLICT: most trackers (Wikipedia citing Bloomberg, Dealroom) date the round to July 2025; Preqin and a Goodwin LLP deal-announcement (Goodwin advised Nudge on the financing, dated 2025-08-04) instead point to early August 2025 -- not reconciled, treat as 'mid-2025.' The Nudge Zero wearable ultrasound headset was unveiled in April 2025, ahead of this raise. Headcount and some other figures still disagree across sources (32-50 employees). Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Non-invasive focused-ultrasound brain interface. First product 'Nudge Zero' in research use as of April 2026; no public security documentation found. Co-founded by Fred Ehrsam (Coinbase co-founder), Jeremy Barenholtz, Quintin Frerichs.

companies.name: Echo Neurotechnologies
companies.funding_note: ~$50M Series A reported 2025-01-30 per Bloomberg ('prominent neurosurgeon Edward Chang has raised about $50 million for a brain implant startup'; described as a16z's first investment in the brain device industry). PitchBook lists investors as A&E Investments, Andreessen Horowitz, and PL Capital. Bloomberg's sourcing was anonymous ('people familiar with the matter'); neither Chang nor a16z has publicly confirmed the figure. Aggregators disagree on the company's founding year (2022 vs. 2023, unresolved). Verified 2026-10-17 (upgraded from a secondary-aggregator-only citation to Bloomberg as primary).
companies.security_notes: Implantable BCI company led by neurosurgeon Edward Chang (UCSF), targeting restoration of communication/movement for people with severe neurological disability. No public security documentation found. Development stage not independently confirmed (no peer-reviewed paper, regulatory filing, or trial report found).

companies.name: Epia Neuro
companies.founded: Public launch/stealth exit: 2026-04-02 (official BusinessWire release). Underlying founding date not independently confirmed.
companies.headquarters: San Francisco, California, USA (per company's own 2026-04-02 BusinessWire launch release, businesswire.com/news/home/20260402282679). A job-listing-based secondary source instead says Alameda -- SF is the better-supported value given the primary press release.
companies.funding_note: No confirmed total. April 2026 public-debut coverage describes a mix of venture and pharmaceutical investment without a disclosed amount. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Minimally invasive skull-implant 'read/write' BCI (non-dura-penetrating) for stroke-related upper-limb motor impairment via a dual-phase stroke therapy pairing the implant, a decoding AI layer, and an external grip-assist glove; planned expansion to cognitive decline. Leadership per company launch release: Michel Maharbiz PhD (CEO; also iota Biosciences co-founder), Gil Mandelbaum PhD (CTO/CSO), Michelle Patruno (COO). Planned first-in-human demonstrations at the Department of Neurosurgery, Lenox Hill Hospital (NY), targeted within 2026 (not yet completed as of this record). No funding amount or employee count confirmed in either verification pass (~45 employees cited only by a single secondary aggregator, not corroborated). No public security documentation found.

companies.name: Kandu, Inc.
companies.founded: Merger announced 2025-04-08 (official BusinessWire release, businesswire.com/news/home/20250408666638; some secondary outlets syndicate this on 2025-04-14). Neurolutions founded 2007; Kandu Health founded 2022 (both confirmed via the official release, resolving the earlier sourcing disagreement on Kandu Health's founding year).
companies.funding_note: $30M first close co-led by Ally Bridge Group and AMED Ventures, confirmed via the official BusinessWire release (2025-04-08) and Fierce Biotech. CONFLICT: CB Insights lists total raised as $9.77M, and a Simplify.jobs listing claims an unconfirmed January 2026 round from K2 HealthVentures and Piper Sandler -- neither reconciled against a primary source; treat $30M as the best-supported figure and the others as unresolved. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Formed by the 2025-04-08 merger of Neurolutions, Inc. (founded 2007; device maker) and Kandu Health, Inc. (founded 2022; post-discharge stroke-recovery support service) under CEO Leo Petrossian (ex-Neurolutions); Kirsten Carroll named CMO of the combined company. IpsiHand (Neurolutions) uses scalp EEG to detect ipsilateral motor intent and drive a hand/arm orthosis; received FDA De Novo clearance in 2021 -- company states this was the first BCI device to receive that clearance (company claim, not independently verified against the FDA database by this session). CMS created a procedure code and benefit-category determination for IpsiHand in 2024. A randomized controlled trial of IpsiHand (Dr. Eric Leuthardt) was reportedly presented at the International Stroke Conference 2026 (New Orleans, Feb 4-6, 2026) showing positive motor-gain results -- secondary-source reporting only, not independently confirmed against conference proceedings. No public device security documentation found.

companies.name: Coherence Neuro
companies.funding_note: $10M seed round closed November 2025, co-led by Artesian and Topology Ventures (joined by Blackbird, Possible Ventures, and others). One secondary aggregator instead lists $13.46M total raised to date -- unresolved discrepancy, not independently reconciled. Verified 2026-10-17 via MassDevice and Seedtable.
companies.security_notes: Coin-sized wireless closed-loop brain implant paired with an over-ear wearable and companion app; targets glioblastoma by recording from and stimulating tumor-adjacent brain tissue to disrupt bioelectric signaling. Founded by Cambridge researchers Ben Woodington and Elise Jenkins; Neuralink head neurosurgeon Matthew MacDougall is an adviser/investor. DEVICE RELATIONSHIP RESOLVED (2026-10-17, via ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07465796, 'A First-in-Human Study of the CIPHER System During Brain Surgery for Newly Diagnosed Glioma'): CIPHER is a bi-directional, flexible electrode-dense thin-film cortical probe used in a short intraoperative (~30 min) first-in-human SAFETY study at Royal Melbourne Hospital, Australia, led by Dr. Andrew Morokoff; registry start 2026-05-22, estimated primary completion 2026-09, target N=10 (press reported 3 patients dosed as of 2026-06-23), two arms (record-only vs. record+stimulate), ages 18-75, newly diagnosed supratentorial glioma. Its purpose is to inform SOMA-1, the company's planned second-generation CHRONIC implant for long-term use -- a later chronic efficacy trial (reported informally as ~2027, not independently confirmed) would be the first real efficacy signal. No public security documentation found for either device.

companies.name: iota Biosciences
companies.funding_note: This figure is acquisition deal consideration, NOT a funding round. $304M = ~$127.5M upfront + up to $176.5M in development milestones (consistent across BioSpace, Fierce Biotech, and Astellas's own press releases: businesswire.com/news/home/20201014006060 announcing the deal 2020-10-15, and newsroom.astellas.com/2020-10-30-Astellas-Completes-Acquisition-of-iota-Biosciences confirming close). BioWorld's larger $429M headline figure adds a separate, non-deal commitment: Astellas pledged up to an additional $125M over 5 years for program growth, on top of (not part of) the $304M acquisition price. iota became a wholly owned Astellas subsidiary effective 2020-10-29 (U.S. Pacific Time). Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: UC Berkeley-originated 'neural dust' technology: millimeter-scale, battery-free, ultrasound-powered wireless implants (Maharbiz/Carmena labs). Astellas and iota held a prior R&D agreement from August 2019 before the 2020 acquisition. No public security documentation found. Retained as an acquired/historical entry for M&A lineage (Astellas).

companies.security_notes: Non-invasive brain-imaging headset using Fast Optical Signals (FOS) to detect when and where neurons fire in real time, described by one profile as sitting 'between EEG and invasive implants.' Stated application areas include epilepsy diagnosis and improving BCI signal quality. Co-founded by Mehmet Gunal (Beckman Institute Cognitive Imaging Lab research affiliate, Foresight Institute-listed). Filed a 'NEURODATA' USPTO trademark application (July 2025, covering brain-derived datasets; non-final office action as of filing) -- note two unrelated 1993 NEURODATA trademarks exist from other companies (Neurodata, Inc. and Washington Neuro Technologies, Inc.), neither connected to BRILL. No funding/investor information found in either verification pass. No public security documentation found. HEADQUARTERS DISPUTED -- see headquarters field.

adjacent_tech.name: Forecast Bio
adjacent_tech.note: NOT a BCI or device company -- an AI/computational biology platform linking cellular neurobiology (astrocyte biology) to mental-health drug effects, founded by UCSF neuroscientist Kira Poskanzer. Selected for the 2026 One Mind Accelerator cohort (official announcement, businesswire.com/news/home/20260209994908, 2026-02-09). FUNDING UNRESOLVED: a Caplight listing shows a $100K accelerator-round investment (dated 2026-03-13); a separate SEC Form D filing reports $2.4M in SAFE financing across 9 investors (first sale 2025-11, $750K of the offering still open as of filing) -- these may be two different instruments (accelerator check vs. a SAFE round) rather than contradictory totals, but this session did not reconcile them. San Francisco, California. Verified 2026-10-17.
adjacent_tech.relevance: Preclinical AI platform modeling drug effects on brain circuits for mental-health therapeutics; relevant to QIF NeuroAI/software threat surface even though it builds no hardware device.
